title: The colimit description of invertible orders
statement:
Let $K$ be a field and $F$ a
torsion sheaf on the etale site
of a $K$-scheme; write $F[n]=\ker(n:F\to F)$ and let $I_K$ be the
set of integers invertible in $K$, as in
[def-kun-torsion-invertible]. Then $F$ has orders invertible in
$K$ if and only if

$$
F=\varinjlim_{n\in I_K}F[n].
$$

The colimit [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] is taken in the category of etale abelian sheaves [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], over the positive integers in $I_K$ ordered by divisibility, with inclusion maps $F[n]\hookrightarrow F[m]$ for $n\mid m$. The kernels are those of [def-pur-abelian-sheaf-kernel]. The displayed equality means that the canonical map $c:\varinjlim_{n\in I_K}F[n]\to F$ induced by the inclusions is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Write $X$ for the $K$-scheme on whose small etale site $F$ is given. The blueprint proof first uses [lemma-weil-pbc-torsion-filtered-union] to identify the unrestricted positive-integer torsion colimit with $F$; the restricted comparison below is the subdiagram needed for the claimed equivalence. By [def-kun-torsion-invertible], $I_K=\{n\geq1:n\cdot1_K\ne0\}$. It contains $1$, and for $n,m\in I_K$ it contains $nm$, since $(nm)\cdot1_K=(n\cdot1_K)(m\cdot1_K)\ne0$ in the field $K$. Thus its divisibility poset is small, nonempty and directed; parallel arrows are unique, so it is a filtered category [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. By [def-pur-abelian-sheaf-kernel], $F[n](U)=\{s\in F(U):ns=0\}$. For $n\mid m$, say $m=an$, $ns=0$ gives $ms=a(ns)=0$, yielding the inclusion $F[n]\hookrightarrow F[m]$. These inclusions compose and are compatible with the inclusions into $F$. All small colimits in $\Ab(X_{\Et})$ exist by [lem-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves-grothendieck], so the colimit universal property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] gives $C=\varinjlim_{n\in I_K}F[n]$ and its canonical comparison $c:C\to F$.

source.place: Blueprint proof opening sentence (unrestricted torsion colimit), together with Tag 03CO (1) for colimit existence and (2) for sectionwise kernels; construction of the restricted diagram is written out here

proof.text: Fix a geometric point $\bar x$ of $X$, with stalk defined in [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks], and put $G=F_{\bar x}$. Exactness of this stalk functor [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact] identifies $(F[n])_{\bar x}\to F_{\bar x}$ with $G[n]=\ker(n:G\to G)\hookrightarrow G$: apply the exact functor to $0\to F[n]\to F\xrightarrow{n}F$. The induced last map is multiplication by $n$, because on a representative section $s$ the germ of $ns$ is $n$ times the germ of $s$. These identifications respect the transition maps: for $n\mid m$ the triangle of inclusions into $F$ commutes, and after taking stalks the map $G[n]\to G[m]$ is the inclusion, since both injections to $G$ send an element to itself.

source.place: Tag 03PT, lemma-stalk-exact (3); compatibility checked on the kernel inclusions

proof.text: For the diagram of subgroups $G[n]\subseteq G$ just obtained, let $U=\bigcup_{n\in I_K}G[n]$. It is a subgroup: two elements killed by $n$ and $m$ have their sum killed by the common multiple $nm\in I_K$, and negatives stay in the same kernel. Its inclusions exhibit $U$ as the colimit [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Indeed, for any compatible family of homomorphisms $f_n:G[n]\to H$, define $f:U\to H$ by $f(x)=f_n(x)$ when $x\in G[n]$. If also $x\in G[m]$, both values equal $f_{nm}(x)$; addition can likewise be checked in $G[nm]$. Thus $f$ is a well-defined homomorphism, and it is uniquely determined because every element of $U$ lies in some $G[n]$. Under this colimit description the comparison to $G$ is exactly the inclusion $U\hookrightarrow G$, so it is an isomorphism if and only if $U=G$.

By [lem-kun-stalks-commute-colimits], $C_{\bar x}\cong\varinjlim_{n\in I_K}(F[n])_{\bar x}$. The colimit isomorphism identifies the stalk $c_{\bar x}$ with the map induced by $(F[n])_{\bar x}\to F_{\bar x}$, because its composites with all colimit coprojections are those stalk inclusions. Combining steps 2 and 3, $c_{\bar x}$ is an isomorphism if and only if every $x\in F_{\bar x}$ is killed by some $n\in I_K$.

source.place: Tag 03PT, lemma-stalk-exact, proof of (1)-(3): directed stalk colimits commute with abelian presheaf colimits and sheafification leaves stalks unchanged; together with Tag 03CO, sites-modules.tex, lemma-limits-colimits-abelian-sheaves (4), this gives preservation of abelian sheaf colimits. Clause (4) of 03PT is stated for sheaves of sets. The comparison is determined by its composites with coprojections.

proof.text: Both $C$ and $F$ are etale sheaves of abelian groups on the same scheme $X$, so [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] applies to $c$: it is an isomorphism if and only if $c_{\bar x}$ is an isomorphism at every geometric point $\bar x$. By step 4 this is equivalent to every element of every geometric stalk being killed by some $n\in I_K$, exactly the condition of having orders invertible in $K$ in [def-kun-torsion-invertible]. This proves both directions for the canonical comparison required in the statement.
